muse2026.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
muse2026.summary: MUSE retains strategic, procedural and tool-use memories around a fixed planning-execution and reflection architecture, without model finetuning. Successful subtask trajectories become reusable procedures; failed attempts trigger diagnosis and replanning, while post-task distillation updates broader guidance. The retained memories, not one completed productivity task, are the reusable harness artifacts. Source: published ACL Findings paper, Sections 2.1-2.4; preprint and proceedings are one study despite changed title and author list.

release.basis: First arXiv submission 2510.08002v1 under Learning on the Job; author publication page links that preprint to the renamed ACL Findings 2026 paper; final metadata follows published PDF

contda2026.summary: ContDa maintains reusable tool documentation as APIs change. Offline relation-guided probing refines descriptions of new tools; relation-aware adjustment groups overlapping tools and adds selection preferences and fallback guidance. Online agents then use the revised documents without parameter training. The tool changes are supplied by the evaluation environment, whereas document revisions are the optimized harness surface; discovery gains do not imply zero forgetting. Source: ACL Findings 2026, Section 4 and Appendix A.8-A.9.

release.basis: ACL Anthology proceedings month; no earlier public preprint verified, so this is a publication-month fallback, not a verified exact first posting date

agentfactory_subagents2026.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
agentfactory_subagents2026.summary: AgentFactory accumulates executable Python subagents in a persistent skill library. A meta-agent allocates tools, creates missing subagents and revises reused ones from execution feedback in task-isolated workspaces; successful subagents are promoted to the shared library and can be exported. Built-in orchestration primitives and tool skills remain fixed. Reusable subagent code is distinct from a task answer and from autonomous rewriting of the supplied meta-agent. Source: ACL 2026 System Demonstrations, Sections 3.1-3.4.

release.basis: First arXiv submission 2603.18000v1; final published ACL demonstration paper and preprint deduplicated as one study

failure_feedback_directedness2026.summary: Evaluates whether failure-guided harness revisions repair their targeted failure rather than merely benefiting after population selection. Public DGM logs show no detectable target-specific advantage in 145 eligible modifications; controlled instruction and helper-code experiments distinguish target repair, collateral breakage and held-out net change. Effects vary with model, editable scope and repairable failure mechanism. This is an evaluation study, not proof that feedback never helps or that all DGM gains are invalid. Source: arXiv:2610.14662v1, Sections 3-5 and 7.4.

release.basis: First arXiv submission; primary submission history lists v1 only when checked, despite a secondary index claiming a later update; no formal venue verified

rsi_two_perspectives2026.summary: A survey organizing agent self-improvement through nine dimensions grouped into update targets, updater organization, schedule and scope, and feedback and acceptance. It connects these design choices to established learning mechanisms and distinguishes online, offline and offline-to-online evaluation. Its taxonomy includes parameter learning alongside memory, skills and code; inclusion here is conceptual background, not an additional demonstrated harness intervention or benchmark finding. Source: arXiv:2610.14625v1, Sections 3-5.

evoharness_rl2026.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
evoharness_rl2026.summary: EvoHarness-RL supplies a Belief-Progress-Experience interface and trains the acting policy through supervised initialization and cost-aware GRPO to choose harness access. Episode-local state differs from reusable Experience: the experience bank is fixed within a rollout batch, then consolidated from outcomes, trajectories and proposed notes using Add, Update, Archive or Skip. The policy weights and persistent experience evolve, not the supplied interface or optimizer code. Source: arXiv:2608.05446v2, Sections 2.1-2.3 and Appendix I.2; workshop acceptance is author-reported.

aide2025.summary: Searches a tree of candidate programs using drafting, debugging, and improvement operators, with a fixed heuristic for parent selection. It is a precursor for search design; its original task-solution search does not itself establish harness self-modification.

aide2_2026.summary: AIDE^2 optimizes a research agent through nested code-search and agent-rewrite loops. The discovered agent changes strategy selection and context management; the main outer driver and incumbent rule remain fixed, with a separate ignition experiment testing an evolved outer driver. Reusing an edited inner codebase is therefore distinguished from automatically replacing the outer rewriter after every update.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

memoharness2026.summary: Organizes harness experience into per-case records and distilled global patterns. Structured retrieval supports search and case-specific deployment adaptation from a frozen training bank without test-time feedback or extra search rounds.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

filesystemmemory2026.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
filesystemmemory2026.summary: Studies management, search, and execution roles around filesystem memory, comparing curated hierarchies, verbatim logs, and chunk retrieval. Organization can reduce retrieval cost without consistently improving correctness, and its sustainability depends on model and tool choices.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

agenttreesearch2024.category: Task-Time Search and Output Refinement (Adjacent Work)
agenttreesearch2024.summary: Applies best-first search over actions in interactive web environments. It provides a task-level search reference for distinguishing planning within one task from search over persistent harness implementations.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

harnesszero2026.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
harnesszero2026.summary: Uses an agent guided by an optimized harness to review and correct student actions in the target harness action space, then fine-tunes the student on the resulting trajectories. The specialized guidance is removed at deployment. This is harness-to-weight distillation, rather than frozen-model harness editing. The reported experiments cover knowledge work, tool use, and science; the training appendix specifies separate domain-specific fine-tuning runs, so the macro-average is not evidence of one jointly trained universal model.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

multitask_selfharness2026.summary: A single-author paper affiliated with Nanjing University. The solver and proposer use the same frozen model and current harness, with the proposer directly editing the code and evolution notes. Evolution mixes five benchmarks, followed by continual adaptation with replay; evaluation includes held-out tasks and five initially unseen benchmarks. Its pretraining/training terminology refers to external harness optimization, not weight updates. Acceptance checks runnability rather than requiring a measured performance improvement. The updated harness is reused by both roles in subsequent iterations, supporting discussion of partial recursion. The execution interface and outer scheduling remain fixed; task-score gains alone do not isolate an improvement in the proposer. This is a central reference for shared solver/proposer harnesses, data mixtures, transfer, and update scheduling.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

dynaharness2026.summary: Connects slower semantic planning with faster physical execution through an explicit execution contract around a frozen VLA. Recorded failures guide changes to reusable capabilities or execution mechanisms, and paired regression checks govern adoption. It supplies a robotics example of failure localization, runtime control, and gated persistent revision; the reported manipulation results do not establish unrestricted self-modification of the optimizer.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

harnessevolve2026.summary: Diagnoses failures by aligning agent trajectories with reference trajectories generated using ground-truth answers, then clusters errors into reusable improvement targets. Separate execution, evaluation, optimization, and gating roles support harness edits. Quality screening targets leakage and prompt growth; performance screening checks current and recent batches, with held-out epoch selection. Relevant to diagnostic feedback and retention, but its privileged reference access must be distinguished from label-free self-evaluation.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

reliable_harness_theory2026.summary: Develops conditions and a validation rule for reliably adopting harness changes while preserving previously successful behavior. It analyzes how verification and evaluation costs limit progress and how observed performance shifts can diagnose stagnation. These are conditional theoretical guarantees, not a universal empirical safety certificate. Version 2, revised September 28, replaces the earlier title Safe Harness Self-Evolution: A Theoretical Analysis of Feasibility and Limits; the two titles denote one paper.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

harness_learning_limits2026.summary: Studies personal-agent harness architecture, scale, and evolution algorithms using a preference-oriented benchmark and a learning-theoretic formulation. Approximation, generalization, and optimization errors organize limits imposed by reachable policies, finite evidence, and biased updates. Useful for explaining why larger harnesses or more evolution rounds need not yield better personalization.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

skillopt2026.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
skillopt2026.summary: Optimizes a skill document as external state of a frozen agent. A separate optimizer converts scored rollouts into bounded add/delete/replace edits, with strict validation improvement required for acceptance. Edit budgets, rejected-edit memory, and slower epoch-level updates connect it to regularization, memory, and scheduling. It is component-level text optimization rather than evidence that the entire harness or optimizer rewrites itself.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

skillissue2026.summary: Builds repository-specific optimization tasks from merged pull requests reverted at a fixed base commit and evaluates the incremental value of a skill document. Across three Kotlin repositories, apparent gains from GEPA are not separable from run-to-run variance at the available sample size, while SkillOpt yields little change. It is useful counterevidence to treating a plausible-looking skill or a small score increase as a reliable improvement.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

r2flow2026.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
r2flow2026.summary: Alternates policy learning, independent verification, and versioned skill-library changes on a shared-state orchestration graph. Separate measures of usage and signed utility prioritize edits, verifier evidence gates them, and a residual-variance plateau controls timing. Library revisions change the graph used by subsequent policy learning. Relevant to coupled learning/evolution, attribution, and scheduling; skill use is explicitly separated from evidence of benefit.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

rsi_onpolicy_distillation2026.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
rsi_onpolicy_distillation2026.summary: Updates a privileged teacher alongside a reasoning student and combines this dynamic co-evolution with training on verified concise rewrites. The teacher receives ground-truth context. This is adjacent model-level self-distillation for mathematical reasoning, included to distinguish weight-space recursion from persistent harness revision rather than as direct evidence of harness RSI.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

liteevo2026.summary: Uses tool-free meta-agents to extract reusable components from execution traces, maintain a versioned library, and compose successive harnesses from a common neutral starting point. It reports both evolution-task results and a separate train/test generalization protocol. Useful for component reuse and optimization cost; sharing a neutral seed across benchmarks should not be confused with evolving one mixed-benchmark harness.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

robot_harness_distillation2026.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
robot_harness_distillation2026.summary: A stronger agent converts intervention experience into a reusable playbook for a lighter robot agent, then revises the playbook using execution feedback. The playbook transfers across agents and manipulation instances without model-weight updates. This is external experience distillation, distinct from the weight distillation of Harness-Zero.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

agent_harness_extraction2026.summary: Studies black-box extraction of another agent system's inference-time harness behavior. An initial inferred harness is refined to match target behavior, and a deception-based defense is evaluated. Included as security and intellectual-property context: its use of distillation concerns behavioral extraction, not Harness-Zero's student-weight training or autonomous improvement of one's own harness.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

hardware_harness_evolution2026.summary: Examines harness evolution around a fixed model on proprietary hardware-verification tasks. Better completion and any-hit coverage do not consistently consolidate into stronger repeatable correctness, and selected validation gains can disappear on replay. A separate repair case study explores cross-benchmark behavior. Relevant to archives, metric choice, regression, and the distinction between complementary specializations and a uniformly better harness.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

last_harness2026.summary: Presents a two-level design: an inner worker/evaluator/editor loop improves a task harness, while an outer loop optimizes the evolution blueprint across tasks. This is a direct conceptual reference for making the improvement procedure an optimization target. Its broad domain-adaptation ambition should not itself be treated as proof of general or unbounded RSI.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

scholarevolve2026.summary: ScholarEvolve draws proposal ideas from research publications rather than relying only on observed task failures and the editor's existing knowledge. It organizes directions by harness module, identifies strategies with topic modeling, and tests implementations and combinations. AppWorld and Tau2-Bench experiments support its research-guided evolution design; the intended ability to ingest future papers is distinct from demonstrating indefinite improvement.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

robot_scale_selection2026.summary: Studies how rollout batch size and candidate selection affect automatically evolved robot-agent harnesses. Relevant to evaluation noise, resource allocation, and regression prevention; repeated use of a fixed selection set remains distinct from held-out assessment.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

evogen_harness2026.summary: Evolves multiple responsibilities outside a frozen image generator. Trace aggregates stochastic execution evidence, uses failure attribution to prioritize candidate changes, and revisits residual failures as components change. A no-update option and held-out validation constrain adoption. It extends the task taxonomy to image generation and illustrates attribution-guided search; it is not evidence of model-weight training.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

videorsi2026.summary: Uses the video agent's own language model to revise its executable observation harness. Active investigation returns to training videos for additional evidence that can distinguish competing failure explanations, rather than relying only on the original trace. Selection considers both answer quality and visual processing cost. It contributes a multimodal example of proposal-time evidence acquisition and cost-aware retention.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

rsigame2026.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
rsigame2026.summary: Combines local exploration, diagnosis, and game revision with a global checkpoint and regression-monitoring loop. An evolving checklist carries testing guidance, and successful development experience is subsequently internalized through training. Included as an application and hybrid-learning reference: revisions to a generated game must be distinguished from revisions to the reusable improvement harness.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

schema2026.summary: Maintains an executable program workspace representing learned environment rules. Interfaces check programs against interaction history, support planning, and verify execution step by step. It is relevant infrastructure for structured experience and environment discovery; revising an environment model within the harness is not automatically revision of the harness optimizer.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

activesaddler2026.summary: Adapts the training curriculum alongside the harness through a non-stationary bandit. Recurrent failures create reusable pattern arms, estimated learning progress changes their priority, and exploration discovers new targets. GAIA2 and Terminal-Bench experiments compare it with the same harness optimizer under a fixed scenario order. It directly informs search, task selection, and experiment allocation; adaptive curriculum control is not necessarily self-rewriting controller code.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

navharness2026.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
navharness2026.summary: Carries maps, task records, and house knowledge between navigation sessions, checking them against new observations and consolidating corrections. Structured recovery handovers and outcome summaries support later reuse without weight training. It provides a recent embodied-memory example, with the distinction that accumulating or correcting task experience does not by itself demonstrate an evolving optimizer.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

coevolving_correction2026.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
coevolving_correction2026.summary: Finds that copying full expert trajectories can degrade a weaker model operating under its evolved harness. The enterprise-task study makes model–harness compatibility a concrete issue in joint evolution, rather than assuming weight and harness improvements add independently.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

minimal_mle_harness2026.summary: Compares elaborate open-source MLE harnesses with a minimal coding-agent session using the same frontier model and time budget. The evaluated systems do not outperform the minimal baseline, and ablations question the value of extra orchestration in those settings. Relevant to budget-matched baselines and complexity; the conclusion is specific to the studied MLE tasks, not a universal rejection of harness engineering.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

coharness2026.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
coharness2026.summary: Alternates harness optimization with model fine-tuning for AI research agents. A HarnessCritic diagnoses failed trajectories and proposes validated local changes; the updated harness generates trajectories for subsequent weight updates. It is a direct joint-optimization reference, useful for contrasting co-evolution with one-way harness distillation and purely frozen-model harness search.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

harbor2026.summary: Formulates harness configuration as constrained noisy Bayesian optimization over a bounded mixed-variable space. A structured surrogate, cost-aware multi-fidelity acquisition, trust regions, and a posterior safety constraint select configurations. It expands the search taxonomy beyond LLM-authored edits and trees, while remaining configuration optimization under a specified search procedure.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

sclate2026.summary: Provides a shared event scheduler for benchmark events and agent-side activity such as session changes and memory consolidation. Its rollout engine supports unmodified harnesses and memory systems, enabling controlled comparisons and model post-training. Relevant to scheduling and evaluation infrastructure; its weight-training results should not be described as autonomous harness-code evolution.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

longhorizon_harness2026.summary: Uses a Manage–Execute–Audit loop with external task state, fresh executor contexts, and a read-only auditor that checks environment facts. Included as harness architecture and verification context; improving execution through this fixed organization is distinct from automatically evolving the organization itself.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

memcodex2026.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
memcodex2026.summary: Rewrites executable memory-layer programs governing construction, indexing, retrieval, and routing. Hierarchical reads proceed from coarse to fine and can fall back to original history. This is directly relevant to evolution of the memory-management procedure, rather than only accumulation of memory contents. The preprint is marked work in progress.

genmem2026.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
genmem2026.summary: Uses stable symbolic identifiers to address memories whose contents can change. A retriever and an evolver learn memory access and revision through GRPO with process and outcome rewards. Relevant to memory addressing and learned management policies; its training component should not be described as purely weight-frozen harness search.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

chime2026.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
chime2026.summary: Separates planning memory from execution memory. Before storing experience, it attributes outcomes to planning, execution, both, or neither, then updates the corresponding bank. It supports discussion of credit assignment and selective memory updates without parameter training; outcome attribution should not be equated with an independently established causal effect.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

selfindex2026.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
selfindex2026.summary: SELF-INDEX diagnoses retrieval failures, selectively revises document index keys, and validates revisions before updating the index. This supplies a concrete example of evolving the retrieval substrate. It is adjacent to harness memory management, not evidence that the complete agent or its optimizer recursively modifies itself.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

cobraskills2026.summary: Formulates skill optimization as budgeted sequential optimization over an evolving candidate population. Contextual bandits prioritize informative or promising evaluations, while execution feedback guides skill revision. It connects search organization to evaluation-budget allocation; the editable objects are reusable skills, not necessarily the entire runtime harness.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

sagegate2026.summary: Compares candidate and incumbent skills on the same validation items. Acceptance requires positive regression-weighted gain, a one-sided paired significance test against the corresponding break-even threshold, and a cap on the fraction of previously solved items that regress. This SAGE is the statistical-gate paper, distinct from other methods with the same acronym.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

sbco2026.summary: Alternates improvements to a decomposed verifier bank and a harness policy through approximate block-coordinate ascent for constrained planning. The meta-agent remains fixed. This is a useful evaluator–policy optimization example and a boundary case separating closed-loop harness improvement from recursive modification of the optimizer.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

selfop2026.summary: Aggregates textual error signals across instances to revise instructions, skills, and reference documents, using cross-instance consensus and a gradient-signal stopping rule. The authors explicitly keep the execution harness and model weights fixed. It belongs in contextual proposal and skill optimization, with this narrower editable scope stated explicitly.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

envrethink2026.summary: Env-Rethink organizes files and evidence through collection maps and event logs, uses a post-trained model to identify environmental noise, and produces changed environments through virtual event histories. This is related environment preparation and evolution, not interchangeable with editing the task-agent harness. This entry records version 1 and its title.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

autorecsys2026.summary: Combines asynchronous experiments, shared cross-server memory, and separation of natural-language skills from deterministic execution scripts. Execution playbooks retain operational experience while an idea loop uses experimental results to guide future proposals. It supports experiment-management and experience-reuse discussions; two loops alone do not establish recursive optimizer evolution.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

seabench2026.summary: Evaluates safety failures emerging from persistent self-evolution across 48 longitudinal task sequences involving instructions, memory protocols, tools, and skills. Paired non-evolving agents support attribution of failures to evolution. Relevant to long-term safety evaluation across update surfaces rather than only immediate task-score gains.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

proctor2026.summary: A position and system report describing evaluation failures in prompt-optimization loops and the PROCTOR architecture. Deterministic gates, role separation, isolated evaluation, frozen holdouts, and canary cases constrain judge-driven updates. Use as a reported design and failure analysis, not a general proof that these safeguards eliminate reward hacking.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

enumgrpo2026.summary: EnumGRPO enumerates agentic query-plan choices and converts quality–cost feedback into reusable planning heuristics through in-context reinforcement learning. It extends workflow-optimization coverage to database queries and cost-aware planning; the term reinforcement learning here should not by itself imply model-weight updates.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

memevolve2025.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
memevolve2025.summary: Jointly evolves experiential knowledge and memory architecture. EvolveLab exposes encoding, storage, retrieval, and management as a modular design space. It provides a direct predecessor for memory-system evolution and distinguishes changes to stored experience from changes to the mechanism that manages it.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

evomemory2025.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
evomemory2025.summary: Evaluates memory across sequential task streams, requiring retrieval and updates after interactions. ExpRAG reuses past experience, while ReMem combines reasoning, actions, and memory refinement. Relevant to measuring continuing adaptation rather than static conversational recall. This entry summarizes version 1; a later version exists.

release.basis: First arXiv submission

reme2025.category: Memory, Context, Skills, and Experience Reuse
reme2025.summary: ReMe distills success patterns, failure triggers, and comparative experience; retrieves through scenario-aware indexing; and refines the pool by adding useful memories and pruning outdated ones. It supports lifecycle-level memory management and procedural experience reuse. ReMe is distinct from the ReMem baseline in Evo-Memory.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

milo2026.summary: Evolves complete agent harnesses using island-based lineage trees, per-island mutators, and an orchestrator. The history retains rejected mutations as negative evidence. When progress stalls, the orchestrator can reassign mutators, graft lineages, preserve niches, and revise the search curriculum. This connects harness search with adaptation of its search configuration. The specified orchestration actions do not by themselves establish recursive rewriting of the orchestrator; capability-level claims require that distinction.

release.basis: First submission recorded in literature map

jitagent2026.summary: Trains a harness generator through customization, repair, and evolution, using a fixed protocol for memory, planning, action, and capability orchestration. Prior configurations and execution feedback support harness adaptation. At deployment the generator remains fixed while traces can guide revisions to harnesses and their archive. It therefore supports discussion of learned proposers and just-in-time adaptation, rather than demonstrating continued recursive training of the generator.

release.basis: First submission recorded in literature map

harde2026.summary: Optimizes a runtime defense harness organized into trigger, monitor, and feedback modules. Isolated module probes first produce an optimization guide; subsequent iterations use safety and benign-task utility feedback to revise the harness. It extends the editable harness beyond task-performance components to runtime risk detection and execution control. Its contribution is safety-aware harness optimization, not evidence that the optimizer recursively rewrites itself.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

harnessrisk2026.category: Benchmarks for Harness Optimization and Adaptation
harnessrisk2026.summary: Introduces a lifecycle-oriented harness-safety benchmark spanning configuration, extension, runtime, persistence, action control, and incident recovery. Sandboxed cases assess utility, attack success, persistence, and detection. The benchmark can inform safety evaluation of evolved harnesses, but it is not itself a harness-improvement algorithm or a dedicated test of recursive improvement.

release.basis: First submission recorded in literature map

harness_disclosure2026.summary: Argues that agent comparisons should disclose their harness and separate model effects from system effects. Its binding-constraint thesis concerns particular long-horizon settings with comparably capable models. This is a methodological position supporting transparent comparison; it should not be cited as experimental proof that harness design universally dominates model capability.

release.basis: First submission recorded in literature map

system_scaling2026.summary: Frames agent capability in terms of system scaling and discusses context governance, trustworthy memory, and dynamic skill routing. It supplies architectural motivation for studying harnesses as an optimization target. Its research agenda is background for this survey, rather than evidence of an implemented recursively self-modifying optimizer.

release.basis: First submission recorded in literature map

hasp2026.category: Model and Policy Training, Harness Co-Evolution, and Distillation
hasp2026.summary: Publication: Accepted to EMNLP 2026 (main conference), as confirmed by the authors' publication lists; final proceedings metadata is not yet confirmed. The summary uses arXiv v2. Represents skills as executable Program Functions that activate in relevant failure states, modify actions, or inject context. These functions support inference-time intervention, training supervision, and controlled skill growth from remaining failures, with executable validation and teacher review. The evolving objects are primarily task-execution skills. They should be distinguished from meta-skills that implement the improvement procedure itself, such as the context-engineering skills evolved by MCE.

release.basis: First submission date from primary-source citation metadata; verified 2026-10-09/10

model_or_harness2026.summary: Localizes agent failures through interaction edges and fault ownership, distinguishing model, harness, environment, and grader failures. The taxonomy provides a vocabulary for deciding whether a failure warrants a harness edit or a different intervention. It supports diagnosis and evaluation design; the taxonomy alone does not implement an autonomous RSI proposal loop.

release.basis: First submission recorded in literature map

primeagent2026.summary: Combines a persistent IPython environment with recursive language-model context processing and a continual harness that retains histories, memory, skills, prompts, and subagents. It is relevant to the state and infrastructure available for continued adaptation. Recursive calls for context processing or subagent execution should not be equated with recursive improvement of the optimizer.

release.basis: First submission recorded in literature map

harness_effects2026.summary: Studies software-engineering agent performance across models, benchmarks, and harnesses, and analyzes components through NanoHarness. The results motivate treating harness effects as dependent on the model and task, rather than assuming that adding components always helps. It provides empirical context for evaluating optimized harnesses, not a recursive harness-optimization method.

release.basis: First submission recorded in literature map

task_aware_harness2026.summary: Matches infrastructure-operation tasks to harness resources using task-to-harness mappings. Map-guided escalation begins with task-specific provision and expands to full provision after a failed self-check. This is useful for comparing runtime configuration with persistent harness evolution. Selecting or escalating a configuration does not alone show that a reusable improvement mechanism has been modified.

release.basis: First submission recorded in literature map

Candidate revisions change one metaskill part and are accepted through validation executions rather than a content-only judge. This is relevant to reusable improvement guidance and generalization, not evidence that any reported whole-system gain is caused by a single rule. Source: arXiv:2609.39148v2, Sections 3-4.
